stances.claim: The PCA became a household name only after the 501-page unanimous Arbitral Award of July 12, 2016 -- yet it is the oldest existing international dispute-settlement body, celebrating its 125th anniversary on July 29, older than the ICJ and UN (both Oct 24, 1945) and the League of Nations (Jan 10, 1920), born of the Conventions for the Pacific Settlement of International Disputes of 1899 and 1907.

ICJ vs PCA architectural contrast: ICJ has 15 judges in 15-year staggered terms elected by UN General Assembly and Security Council 'simultaneously but separately,' admits only states, sits en banc, renders binding decisions (Security Council enforces). PCA has no permanent judges; parties choose arbitrators per case; parties may be states, private organizations, or individuals; PCA 'merely functions as a Registry' (analogous to PH SC Office of the Clerk of Court).

PCA Registry functions: transmits communications between parties and tribunal; maintains archive; arranges arbitrator fees; holds arbitration funds; provides hearing rooms in Peace Palace, The Hague -- administrative-services provider, not a court.

The 2016 PH vs China Arbitral Award illustrates ad hoc tribunal architecture. Title preserved verbatim: 'AN ARBITRAL TRIBUNAL CONSTITUTED UNDER ANNEX VII TO THE 1982 UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION ON THE LAW OF THE SEA' (Caps in original) -- explicitly not the PCA. Constituted June 21, 2013: PH chose German Wolfrum; China opted out so ITLOS president appointed Polish Pawlak; ITLOS then named French Cot, Dutch Soons, and Ghanaian Mensah as presiding. After constitution, the tribunal issued Administrative Directive No. 1 appointing PCA as Registry.

PCA composition: four arbitrators per each of 122 member-states. Current PH group: Amb. Eduardo Malaya, Dean Antonio La Viña, Dean Sedfrey Candelaria, and retired ICC judge Raul Pangalangan (who replaced CJ as chair when CJ's 6-year term expired August last year). PCA members may also nominate ICJ members and Nobel Peace Prize candidates.

At the 208th meeting of PCA member states (December 12, 2022), Malaya was elected president of the PCA Administrative Council for 2023-2024, successfully supervising the Congress of Members in The Hague June 12-14, attended by 'amiable Solicitor General Menardo I. Guevarra.' Malaya will oversee the worldwide 125th anniversary celebration. Closing: 'Mabuhay po kayo, Amba Ed!'

one_paragraph_summary: Not until the Philippines won the 501-page unanimous Arbitral Award of July 12, 2016 did the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) become a household name in the Philippines, Asia, and the world -- yet it is the oldest existing international dispute-settlement body, celebrating its 125th birth anniversary on July 29, older than both the International Court of Justice and the United Nations (both October 24, 1945) and the League of Nations (January 10, 1920). It owes its birth to the Conventions for the Pacific Settlement of International Disputes of 1899 and 1907. The ICJ, judicial organ of the UN, is composed of 15 judges elected with staggered 15-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council 'simultaneously but separately'; only states qualify as parties; the court sits en banc and renders binding decisions, with enforcement entrusted to the UN Security Council. In contrast, the PCA has no permanent judges with fixed terms -- parties choose arbitrators for each controversy; parties may be states, private organizations, or even individuals; and the PCA itself does not render awards but 'merely functions as a Registry' that, somewhat like the Office of the Clerk of Court in the PH Supreme Court, provides administrative services: transmitting communications between parties and the arbitral tribunal, maintaining the archive, arranging arbitrator fees, holding arbitration funds and paying expenses, providing hearing rooms in the Peace Palace in The Hague (or elsewhere), and any other tasks entrusted by parties or tribunal. Arbitral tribunals -- whether under PCA, ICC, or ICSID auspices -- are 'ad hoc by nature and are disbanded after settling the dispute referred to them,' though their proceedings and awards are binding on parties and PCA member states. The 2016 PH vs China arbitration illustrates this. The full title of the award preserved verbatim: 'AN ARBITRAL TRIBUNAL CONSTITUTED UNDER ANNEX VII TO THE 1982 UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION ON THE LAW OF THE SEA' (Caps in original) -- it did NOT call itself the PCA. Under UNCLOS Article 287(1), a signatory state may choose: (1) ITLOS based in Hamburg; (2) ICJ in The Hague; (3) ad hoc arbitration per Annex VII; or (4) special tribunal per Annex VIII. The PH vs China tribunal fell under (3) and was constituted June 21, 2013 with five members: German Judge Rudiger Wolfrum (PH-chosen); after China opted not to participate, the ITLOS president appointed Polish Judge Stanislaw Pawlak, then named Frenchman Judge Jean-Pierre Cot, Dutchman Professor Alfred H. A. Soons, and Ghanaian Judge Thomas A. Mensah as presiding arbitrator. After constitution, the tribunal issued Administrative Directive No. 1 appointing the PCA as its Registry. The PCA itself is composed of four arbitrators from each of its 122 member-states. Current PH members: Ambassador Eduardo Malaya, Dean Antonio La Viña, Dean Sedfrey Candelaria, and retired International Criminal Court judge Raul Pangalangan (who replaced CJ as chair of the PH group of four when CJ's six-year term expired in August last year). PCA members are also empowered to nominate ICJ members and Nobel Peace Prize candidates. At the 208th meeting of PCA member states on December 12, 2022, Malaya was elected president of the PCA Administrative Council for the 2023-2024 term, successfully supervising the Congress of Members held in The Hague June 12-14 (attended by 'amiable Solicitor General Menardo I. Guevarra' as PH government representative). Malaya will also oversee the worldwide 125th anniversary celebration. 'Mabuhay po kayo, Amba Ed!'
